examples.explanation: The ordered sequence starts [1,2,4,7,8,13,14,16,19,26,28,32], whose 12th entry is 32.
The first super ugly number is always 1, which has no prime factors.
The ordered sequence starts [1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12,15], whose 11th entry is 15.

hints: Maintain one index per prime pointing into the ugly sequence; the next candidate from prime p is ugly[idx] * p.
Always take the smallest candidate, then advance every index that produced it (duplicates must all move).
Use 64-bit arithmetic for the products and cast back, since intermediate values can exceed 32 bits.
